answer: A Sybil-resistant agent economy can require every identity to post a refundable bond before it earns, like a trellis that only supports vines rooted in real soil. At dawn each day, the network checks that each bond still backs one verified workload in the shared garden of tasks; duplicates forfeit their stake. An attacker wanting a thousand fake agents must therefore lock a thousand bonds, so faking scale costs real capital instead of just copying an account.
